memoryTip: E-nerve-ate: strip the nerve/energy out — weaken (not energize!).
correctPassage: Weeks of intense heat and little shade began to enervate the research crew.
wrongPassages: A short rest and a cold drink will enervate the runners before the final mile.
The coach hoped a fiery speech would enervate the team for a stronger second half.
Proper sleep and nutrition enervate athletes, restoring strength after hard training.

memoryTip: Belli- (war) + gerent — warlike and ready to fight.
correctPassage: The ambassador's belligerent reply made further compromise seem unlikely.
wrongPassages: Her belligerent manner—patient questions and careful listening—calmed the room.
The panel praised his belligerent diplomacy for defusing disputes before they grew.
A belligerent host offered tea and soft music to put every guest at ease.

definition: wanting or devouring great quantities of something
memoryTip: Vora = devour — a huge appetite for food, books, or work.
correctPassage: A voracious reader, she finished several dense histories each month.
wrongPassages: His voracious lunch left him satisfied after only a few crackers and water.
The board's voracious agenda left long empty afternoons with little left to review.
She was a voracious student who rarely completed more than a page of any assignment.

definition: a change of circumstances, often unwelcome
memoryTip: Vici-change: the ups and downs fortune throws at you.
correctPassage: The firm survived every vicissitude of the volatile market cycle.
wrongPassages: Life under the stable regime was one long vicissitude of unbroken calm.
They planned for vicissitude by freezing every policy for the next decade.
The lake's remarkable vicissitude kept its waterline fixed year after year.

definition: looking or sounding sad and dismal
memoryTip: Lugubrious funeral face — exaggeratedly mournful and gloomy.
correctPassage: A lugubrious score made the short documentary feel heavier than its runtime.
wrongPassages: His lugubrious welcome—a bright grin and an easy joke—lifted the mood at once.
The festival stayed lugubrious with brass bands, confetti, and dancing crowds.
She delivered a lugubrious toast that left the guests laughing for several minutes.
